title: [YouPass Collect] - Train passenger numbers and punctuality trends: 2000-2009
prompt: The first graph shows the number of train passengers from 2000 to 2009. The second graph shows the percentage of trains running on time.
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graphs illustrate the number of train passengers and the percentage of trains running on time over a nine-year period from 2000 to 2009.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, both the number of train users and the percentage of services running on schedule showed fluctuating patterns throughout the period. Notably, passenger numbers peaked in the middle of the period, while punctuality rates eventually exceeded the target in the later years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at passenger figures, there were 36 million rail users in 2000. This number then increased to approximately 41 million in 2001 and around 42 million by 2002, before dropping sharply back to 36 million in 2003. Following this decline, passenger volumes recovered to roughly 41 million in 2004 and reached a peak of 46 million in 2005. After this high point, the figures fell to about 42 million in 2006 and remained at this level in 2007. Numbers then declined further to approximately 40 million in 2008, before recovering slightly to around 42 million in 2009.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding punctuality performance, 92% of trains operated on time in 2000, falling 3 percentage points short of the 95% target. The rate subsequently improved to around 94% in 2001, meeting the target at 95% in 2002. It continued to rise, reaching slightly above 95% in 2003 and peaking at 96% in 2004. However, performance deteriorated to just below 95% in 2005 and dropped to its lowest point of 92% in 2006, matching the starting figure. From 2007, punctuality rates began to recover to approximately 93%, and by 2008, they had surged dramatically to 97%, exceeding the target for the first time. This level was maintained through 2009, remaining 2 percentage points above the target.
